hints: Focus on splitting each ester name into its acid part and its alcohol part, the second word tells you about P and the first word tells you about Q.
A carboxylic acid with no possible branched chain must be very short, so check which acids are propanoic or ethanoic with 3 carbons or fewer.
Now compare the alcohols left, a straight C4 alcohol has just two OH positions while a straight C5 alcohol has three, so only one of them fits having just one positional partner.
walkthrough:
**Split the ester into acid + alcohol**

Remember ester formation is acid + alcohol. The second word comes from the acid, the first word comes from the alcohol.

For example:
$$\text{butyl propanoate = butanol + propanoic acid}$$

**Use the no chain isomers clue for acid P**

Chain isomerism needs enough carbons to make a branched skeleton. $\text{C}_1$, $\text{C}_2$ and $\text{C}_3$ acids cannot branch.

$$\text{methanoic, ethanoic, propanoic = no chain isomers}$$

$$\text{butanoic, pentanoic = have branched chain isomers}$$

So P must be ethanoate or propanoate. That leaves only butyl propanoate and pentyl ethanoate as possible.

**Use the one positional isomer clue for alcohol Q**

Positional isomerism for alcohols means moving the $\text{-OH}$ to a different carbon. Ethanol has only one possible position, so it has no positional isomer.

Propan-1-ol has one partner, propan-2-ol. Butan-1-ol has one partner, butan-2-ol. Pentan-1-ol has two partners, pentan-2-ol and pentan-3-ol.

So a $\text{C}_4$ alcohol fits the one positional isomer description, but a $\text{C}_5$ alcohol does not.

**Conclude the ester**

Propanoic acid fits P with no chain isomers, and butanol fits Q with only one positional isomer. Together they make butyl propanoate.

options.A: Correct. Propanoate means P is propanoic acid, $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{COOH}$, which is too short to have a branched chain isomer. Butyl means Q is butanol, $\text{C}_4\text{H}_9\text{OH}$, where butan-1-ol has just one straight-chain positional partner, butan-2-ol. Both conditions are satisfied.
options.B: Incorrect. Ethyl means Q is ethanol, which has no positional isomer at all, not one. Butanoate means P is butanoic acid, which does have a chain isomer, 2-methylpropanoic acid. It fails both clues.
options.C: Incorrect. This is the tempting trap. Ethanoate means P is ethanoic acid, which correctly has no chain isomers. However, pentyl means Q is pentanol, where pentan-1-ol has two positional isomers, pentan-2-ol and pentan-3-ol, not one. So it fails the alcohol clue.
options.D: Incorrect. Propyl means Q is propanol, which correctly has one positional isomer. However, pentanoate means P is pentanoic acid, $\text{C}_5$, which has several branched chain isomers such as 2-methylbutanoic acid and 2,2-dimethylpropanoic acid. So it fails the acid clue.
